method: A box score does not record possessions directly, so they are estimated from the events that end one. Field goal attempts each end a possession, and offensive rebounds are subtracted because a put-back keeps the same possession alive. Turnovers are added. Free throw attempts count as 0.44 of a possession on average: a single free throw ends a possession when missed, but the last of two or three is often made and the resulting rebound is usually a dead-ball team rebound, so a pair of free throws is worth about 0.88 possessions rather than two. The estimate is FGA + 0.44*FTA - OREB + TOV. Points per possession is points divided by that estimate, offensive rating is the same figure per 100 possessions, pace rescales possessions to a 48-minute game, and turnover rate is turnovers divided by field goal attempts plus 0.44 times free throw attempts plus turnovers. A line of 105 points on 85 field goal attempts, 25 free throw attempts, 10 offensive rebounds and 14 turnovers gives 85 + 11 - 10 + 14 = 100 possessions, 1.05 points per possession, an offensive rating of 105.0, a pace of 100 over 48 minutes and a turnover rate of 12.7 percent; the same arithmetic on 78 points, 60 attempts, 20 free throws, 8 offensive rebounds and 12 turnovers over 40 minutes gives 72.8 possessions, 1.071 points per possession, an offensive rating of 107.1, a pace of 87.4 and a turnover rate of 14.9 percent. Counts are whole numbers limited to a plausible box-score range (points 0 to 250, field goal attempts 1 to 150, free throw attempts 0 to 100, offensive rebounds and turnovers 0 to 60, game length 1 to 60 minutes); text, decimals, negatives, exponent notation, out-of-range values and counts that would imply zero or negative possessions are refused with the field named. This is the standard box-score estimator, not an official count: it does not separate team from individual rebounds, ignores possessions that end without a shot, free throw or turnover, and treats the 0.44 factor as constant. The page calculates locally and stores, uploads and transmits nothing.

sources.title: Basketball analytics glossary: possessions are estimated as FGA + 0.44*FTA - OREB + TOV, the standard box-score approximation of Dean Oliver.
Basketball analytics practice: offensive rating is points scored per 100 possessions and pace is possessions scaled to a 48-minute game.
